title: Sgraffito two-colour slip technique
subtitle: Scratching through a coloured slip layer to reveal contrasting clay beneath
excerpt: Sgraffito on a two-colour slip surface works by painting one coloured slip over a piece, letting it reach leather-hard stage, then scratching through the slip to reveal the base clay colour. The result is a line drawing in the colour of the base clay against a contrasting slip background.
sourceNotes: Sgraffito technique from traditional earthenware slip decoration; used across Mediterranean and Central European folk pottery traditions. Technique derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: Scratching through a slip layer to reveal the contrasting clay body beneath; from the Italian word for scratched
Clay diluted with water to a brushable consistency; tinted with clay stain or coloured clay for decorative layers
The ideal stage for sgraffito: the slip layer is firm enough to scratch without smearing but the clay is still slightly damp
Unfired clay in any drying stage before any heat treatment

content.text: Sgraffito
on a coloured
slip
surface is a line-drawing technique applied to
greenware
. A coloured slip is applied to the piece's surface, dried to
leather-hard
, then scratched away in lines to reveal the contrasting base clay beneath. The technique works equally on air-dry clay (no kiln) and on stoneware before bisque firing.
When to use this technique

Sgraffito suits flat tile surfaces, bowl interiors, and pot exteriors where a drawn line pattern is wanted. It works best when the slip and the base clay have contrasting values: dark slip over light clay, or white slip over a red earthenware or terracotta-tinted clay.
What you need
A leather-hard clay piece , tile, bowl, or pot
Coloured slip , air-dry clay thinned to a brushable consistency and tinted with a powdered acrylic pigment or iron oxide
A liner brush for applying the slip
A sgraffito tool or a stiff needle for scratching
A soft brush to clear loose clay dust from the scratched lines
Step-by-step

Apply one to two coats of coloured slip over the surface of the leather-hard piece using a broad liner brush. Each coat should be thin enough to see the base clay colour through it. Two thin coats build a consistent colour layer better than one thick coat, which may crack.

Allow the slip to dry to leather-hard , firm to the touch but not powdery. This usually takes 30-60 minutes in a normal room. The right stage: the tip of a sgraffito tool draws a clean line that does not smear at the edges.

Scratch the design into the slip surface with a sgraffito tool or stiff needle. Draw the design lightly first as a sketch, then go over the lines with more pressure to clear the slip down to the base clay. Keep lines consistent in depth , going through the base clay itself breaks the surface.
Brush away loose clay dust from the scratched lines with a dry soft brush. The contrast between the slip layer and the base clay colour is now visible.
Allow the piece to dry fully at room temperature. Seal with PVA varnish for air-dry clay, or proceed to bisque firing for stoneware.
What it looks like when it is right

Correct sgraffito lines are clean, with crisp edges and the base clay colour visible at the bottom of each scratch. The slip on either side of the line stays flat and undisturbed. Lines drawn when the slip was too wet leave smeared edges; lines drawn when too dry flake the slip off in chips rather than cutting cleanly.
Common mistakes
Scratching when the slip is too wet. The tool pushes slip to the line edges and creates raised ridges. Wait until the slip feels the same as the base clay under a light touch.
Scratching when the slip is too dry. Dry slip chips away in fragments rather than cutting in a controlled line. Work the slip slightly damper next time.
Applying slip too thickly. A thick slip layer cracks as it dries, particularly on curved surfaces. Apply two thin coats rather than one thick coat.
Scratching through the base clay. Over-deep lines weaken the piece. For air-dry clay, fill deep accidental cuts with fresh slip and allow to dry before re-scratching.
